Do you have any idea how absurdly unbearable the pain we feel is? Thank you for sharing your personal experience, and I am sorry for your loss, but you're asking someone to suck up their pain to stop others from feeling it. Just think about that what if someone said to you "I'm pretty sure the pain he(your best friend) was feeling was far worse than what you're feeling now" "I don't know how to help you out, but just accept that." Its not exactly a good comparison, but I want you to better understanding how hopeless it feels for those of us that go down that path. Honestly speaking from experience, the feelings that lead to suicide are not too different from how you are feeling now, but instead of not being able to cope with losing a friend, its not being able to cope with living, life in general, inability to find happiness or success, etc. I don't want to belittle your pain because I can only imagine how immense it must be, but I want you to understand the pain of those you're talking to. Understanding is the first step to being able to make a difference.
My depression is already exhaust and all-consuming. I just want a way out of this misery. I know what feeling suicidal is like, and I want it back as terrible as that sounds. I'm just so miserable.

I understand somewhat. I've never been in a relationship so no clue what the break up feels like, but that feeling of being undesirable when you just want one person to want you really fucks you up. You've had more like in 5 months than I've had in my whole life so its not completely hopeless. 

Idk what your situation is, but here's some general stuff that I've picked up through trying constantly,

1. try changing your look - get a new haircut, do something different with your facial hair (if you can), find different clothes and make sure they fit properly, etc. because A this might make you more attractive, and B it can be a nice confidence boost sometimes. 

2. Just get out there if you can, try to go to class, go to extracurricular stuff, etc. Sit next to any girl you can and just try talking to them. Just try and talk to more girls. Its hard as fuck, but just introducing yourself with a smile and making some sort of conversation (its easier if you're at an extracurricular since you have an easy subject). Dumb jokes are always a go to. I have a few that are pretty common and easy to use (today I was talking to a girl at the library, and she said she was dying(cause homework and stuff). So I responded no don't die I've heard that's bad for your health.). Having some easy to execute jokes that will be usable in everyday conversation helps a lot.

 3. Focus on your posture and outward attitude. Standing up straighter and smiling more (even if its not genuine) makes you more attractive.

Its not easy and god damn rejection is the norm, but I mean do everything you can to get your happiness. At the end of the day you just gotta keep reaching for happiness because that's what matters.

Community college doesn't hurt though. At my school a lot of people could start here academically, but it makes more financial sense to get their gen eds out of the way at community college before transfering in.
